items.text:
"Deep systems, slow burn — worth it if you're patient"

I found this game while looking for something with deep vehicle customization and a living world around it. Ostranauts delivers on both fronts, but it earns your attention rather than handing it to you.
The ship customization is genuinely impressive in scope — there's a lot to learn, and the game doesn't hold your hand. Space travel has a weight to it that feels different from most games in the genre. That said, after 10 hours I've barely scratched the surface, still hanging around K-Leg and figuring out systems. Whether that's a feature or a barrier will depend entirely on your patience for slow-burn gameplay.

Steam Deck performance is serviceable. Some occasional lag spikes, and the controller layout gets you most of the way there — but a few things still feel like they want a mouse and keyboard. Not a dealbreaker, but worth knowing before you commit to handheld-only.
If you're the kind of player who likes pulling at threads and building your own momentum, it's easy to recommend.
items.text_zh:
“深度系统，慢热——如果你有耐心，就值得”

我在寻找一款有深度载具自定义以及围绕它的鲜活世界的游戏时发现了这款游戏。Ostranauts在这两方面都做到了，但它是靠赢得你的注意力，而不是直接把注意力塞给你。
飞船自定义的规模确实令人印象深刻——有很多要学，而且游戏不会手把手教你。太空旅行有一种厚重感，感觉和这个类型里大多数游戏都不一样。话虽如此，玩了10个小时后我也才刚摸到皮毛，还在K-Leg附近晃悠，研究各种系统。这到底算优点还是门槛，完全取决于你对慢热玩法的耐心。

Steam Deck性能还算能用。偶尔会有卡顿峰值，手柄布局能让你完成大部分操作——但有些东西仍然感觉需要鼠标和键盘。不是致命问题，但在你决定只用掌机玩之前值得知道。
如果你是那种喜欢顺藤摸瓜、自己积累动力的玩家，那很容易推荐。
